src: USD/TWD (TWD=X), TAIEX (^TWII, gaps filled from TWSE MI_5MINS_HIST), dollar index and USD/KRW: Yahoo Finance daily closes. Foreign investor net buy: TWSE 三大法人買賣金額統計表 (BFI82U), foreign and mainland investors excluding foreign dealers, TWD bn.

notes.headline: Foreigners have sold TWD 963bn of Taiwan stocks in 20 sessions, the heaviest stretch since July's TWD 1.0trn peak, and USD/TWD is up 2.2% in 20 days to 32.48. Friday's TWD 112.5bn of selling pushed the short-term pressure signal further onto the long USD/TWD side, and history says don't fade a selling wave.
notes.now: Foreigners sold TWD 112.5bn of shares on Friday, the heaviest day since mid-October, as a global AI selloff after disappointing US tech results knocked the TAIEX down 2.5% to near correction territory. Selling pressure rose to +1.45 from +0.88, well above the +0.5 trigger, so the long USD/TWD signal set on Oct 29 stays on, with an edge that lasts one to two days. The one-month exhaustion gauge deepened to −1.86 in 'outflows stretched', an episode now seven sessions old, but that side worked only 3 times in 9, so it is not a reason to short. The dollar index is down 0.2% over 20 days and US yields fell on the risk-off move, so this is a Taiwan flow story, which the central bank governor also blamed on foreign profit-taking this week while saying it does not defend a set level. Onshore, the US dollar traded near 32.67 on Friday morning, above Yahoo's 32.48 close, so stay long USD/TWD into early next week.
notes.flip: Back to neutral if selling pressure falls under +0.5 again. A short USD/TWD (stronger TWD) case needs foreigners to turn steady buyers: selling pressure at or below −0.5 for several sessions, with the TAIEX recovering toward its record.
findings: Flows and the TWD move together
Over 5-day windows, foreign net buying and USD/TWD have a −0.47 correlation: when foreigners sell Taiwan stocks, the TWD weakens in the same week. This is why the link looks so strong on a chart.

Foreign investors convert currency around settlement (T+2), so a heavy selling day tends to keep pushing USD/TWD up for a day or two. Acting at the close on the day TWSE posts the flows, the pressure signal had an information coefficient of 0.21 and a Sharpe of 1.9 over two years. One day later it drops to 0.08 and 0.8, so it has to be acted on quickly. It isn't just the May 2025 surge: leaving out April–June 2025, the same-day version still made +14% with a Sharpe of 2.2.
After a month of heavy buying, the TWD gives back gains

When foreigners had been heavy buyers for 20 sessions and the TAIEX was strong (exhaustion ≥ +1), USD/TWD rose over the next month in 11 of 14 episodes, by 1.1% on average. That fits the central bank smoothing TWD strength and exporters and life insurers selling dollars less aggressively.
After a month of heavy selling, there is no rebound edge

The mirror case did not work: after heavy selling (exhaustion ≤ −1), the TWD rebounded in only 3 of 9 episodes, and the one big win was the May 2025 TWD surge, driven by life-insurer hedging rather than equity flows. So the dashboard treats 'outflows stretched' as a warning, not a call to short USD/TWD.
notes.caveats: Two years is a short sample: the one-month results rest on about two dozen independent 20-day windows, and the long side was helped by USD/TWD's climb from 29 to 32 since mid-2025. Flows here are TWSE-listed shares only (no TPEx, no bond or insurer flows), and USD/TWD is Yahoo's daily close, which can differ from the 4pm Taipei onshore close. Results ignore trading costs and carry (USD/TWD forward points cost a long-USD position roughly 0.15–0.2% a month, the US–Taiwan rate gap). A research signal, not financial advice.
